# Spinner

Progress with no known duration.

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@kafka/react'
```

## When to use it

- A short wait whose length you can't tell: loading a section, saving.
- Inside a region that updates; use Skeleton when the layout is known.

## When not to

- When you know the percentage: use Progress.
- Inside a button: use the Button's loading state.

## Examples

### Sizes

It announces "Cargando" by default. Under reduced motion it turns slowly instead of stopping, so it still reads as "in progress".

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
  <Spinner size="sm" />
  <Spinner />
  <Spinner size="lg" />
</div>
```

### Specific label

Say what is happening when "Cargando" is too vague.

```tsx
<Spinner label="Guardando tu inscripción…" />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `SpinnerSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  | What is happening, announced to screen readers. Defaults to the localised "Loading". |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **A `role="status"` with a text name** ("Cargando"), so it is announced; pass `label` for something more specific.
- **Reduced motion:** it turns slowly instead of stopping, so it still reads as "in progress".
- The arc is 3:1 against the page and against a surface, in both modes.

## Content

- The label says what is happening: "Guardando tu inscripción…".
